mini.icons

### Question

Hi there,

I'm trying to slot mini.icons in for nvim_web_devicons in https://github.com/utilyre/barbecue.nvim and not having any luck. Here is how I am attempting to use it:

```lua
return {
  "utilyre/barbecue.nvim",
  name = "barbecue",
  version = "*",
  dependencies = {
    "SmiteshP/nvim-navic",
    "echasnovski/mini.icons",
  },
  config = function()
    require("mini.icons").setup()
    MiniIcons.mock_nvim_web_devicons()
  end,
  opts = {
    theme = "tokyonight",
    show_modified = true,
    show_navic = false,
    create_autocmd = true,
  },
}
```

Anything obviously wrong here? Thanks in advance.

comment_data.body:
You can use the following code to simulate `nvim-web-devicons` using `MiniIcons`, as if it were a substitute:  

```lua
package.preload["nvim-web-devicons"] = function()
    package.loaded["nvim-web-devicons"] = {}
    MiniIcons.mock_nvim_web_devicons()
    return package.loaded["nvim-web-devicons"]
end
```  

This will make `nvim-web-devicons` appear as if it's being provided by MiniIcons.

Here is [the full example of usage](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/7c0e12076af6a45227273b57110a91e9089a93fc/doc/mini-icons.txt#L472-L476). Just calling it after `require('mini.icons').setup()` is enough (as you have in your code)

The reason you don't see effect in 'barbecue.nvim' is due to its special (and as far as I am aware - not entirely robust/correct) usage of 'nvim-web-devicons'. See #1207 and #1265.

reply_data.body:
> I apologize if I do not understand _lazy.nvim_ and _mini.icons_ correctly but I think the given example is a bit misleading ...

The example is not about any particular plugin manager. It shows what needs to be done in order to mock 'nvim-web-devicons'.

About the linked example and 'lazy.nvim' setup... I think [what you posted](https://github.com/nvim-lualine/lualine.nvim/issues/1378#issuecomment-3824191931) is the correct approach to handle this. If some plugin is declared as a dependency and needs custom setup, then it is a good idea to add its specification separately. My suggestion would even be to just drop the whole `opts.mock_nvim_web_devicons = true` part and just have `require('mini.icons').setup()` and `MiniIcons.mock_nvim_web_devicons()` in 'mini.icons' setup. I.e. the full example of usage linked earlier.

---

And by the way, it is 'nvim-mini/mini.icons' now, not 'echasnovski/mini.icons'. Shouldn't be a problem for some time now, but it is a good idea to adjust now.
